This chapter teaches the words for pointing at things: **this / that** — ده (da), دي (di) and دول (dol) — and how to name the objects around you. Tap any sentence to reveal its franco and English.

## How it works

**One set covers both "this" and "that".** Egyptian doesn't split them: **ده (da)** for a masculine thing, **دي (di)** for a feminine thing, **دول (dol)** for plural — used for near *and* far alike. A gesture or the word **هناك (henak)** "there" marks distance when you need it.

**Two structures, and the contrast matters:**

- **After a noun** (the noun takes ال): **الكتاب ده (el-ketab da)** = "this book". Here the demonstrative is just describing.
- **At the front, as the subject:** **ده كتاب (da ketab)** = "this **is** a book". Egyptian has no verb "to be", so the bare demonstrative + noun already means "this is…".

So *el-ketab da* (this book) and *da ketab* (this is a book) are different sentences — watch the word order.

**Asking:** **ده إيه؟ (da eh?)** / **دي إيه؟ (di eh?)** = "what's this?".

**Whose is it — بتاع (betaa3).** To say "mine / yours", use بتاع, which agrees with the thing owned and then takes an ending: **الكتاب ده بتاعي (el-ketab da bta3i)** "this book is mine"; for a feminine thing, بتاعتي (bta3ti).

## Demonstratives

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| ده - da | this / that (m.) |
| دي - di | this / that (f.) |
| دول - dol | these / those (pl.) |
| هنا - hena | here |
| هناك - henak | there |

## Objects around you

**Clothes**

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| قميص - 2amis (m.) | shirt |
| فستان - fustan (m.) | dress |
| جزمة - gazma (f.) | shoes |

**Furniture**

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| ترابيزة - tarabeza (f.) | table |
| كرسي - korsi (m.) | chair |
| سرير - sereer (m.) | bed |

**Animals**

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| كلب - kalb (m.) | dog |
| قطة - 2otta (f.) | cat |
| حصان - 7osan (m.) | horse |

**Everyday things**

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| كتاب - ketab (m.) | book |
| قلم - 2alam (m.) | pen |
| شنطة - shanta (f.) | bag |
| موبايل - mobile (m.) | phone |
| ساعة - sa3a (f.) | watch / clock |

## Using demonstratives in a sentence

For "I want / I see / it's mine" you can use a couple of words that just agree in gender (the full verbs come in their own chapters). Negate them with **مش (mesh)**.

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| عايز / عايزة - 3ayez / 3ayza | wanting (m. / f.) |
| شايف / شايفة - shayef / shayfa | seeing (m. / f.) |

<details class="frase">
<summary>عايز الكرسي ده</summary>
<span class="fr">3ayez el-korsi da</span>
<span class="en">I want this chair</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>شايف الحصان هناك</summary>
<span class="fr">shayef el-7osan henak</span>
<span class="en">I see that horse (over there)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>الشنطة دي بتاعتي</summary>
<span class="fr">el-shanta di bta3ti</span>
<span class="en">this bag is mine</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>مش عايز القميص ده</summary>
<span class="fr">mesh 3ayez el-2amis da</span>
<span class="en">I don't want this shirt</span>
</details>

## Dialogue: "What's this?"

Sherif is looking around Nadia's place.

<span class="rotulo">شريف — Sherif</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>ده إيه؟</summary>
<span class="fr">da eh?</span>
<span class="en">What's this?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">نادية — Nadia</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>ده موبايل</summary>
<span class="fr">da mobile</span>
<span class="en">It's a phone</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">شريف — Sherif</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>الموبايل ده بتاعك؟</summary>
<span class="fr">el-mobile da bta3ek?</span>
<span class="en">Is this phone yours?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">نادية — Nadia</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>لأ، ده مش بتاعي. ده بتاع أختي</summary>
<span class="fr">la2, da mesh bta3i. da bta3 o5ti</span>
<span class="en">No, it's not mine. It's my sister's</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">شريف — Sherif</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>والقطة دي؟</summary>
<span class="fr">wel-2otta di?</span>
<span class="en">And this cat?</span>
</details>

<span class="rotulo">نادية — Nadia</span>
<details class="frase">
<summary>أيوة، دي بتاعتي</summary>
<span class="fr">aywa, di bta3ti</span>
<span class="en">Yes, she's mine</span>
</details>

### Exercise 1 — ده، دي or دول؟

Choose the demonstrative that agrees with the noun.

**1.** الكتاب ___ *(book, m.)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">ده</span>
<span class="fr">el-ketab da</span>
</details>

**2.** الترابيزة ___ *(table, f.)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">دي</span>
<span class="fr">el-tarabeza di</span>
</details>

**3.** الكلاب ___ *(dogs, pl.)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">دول</span>
<span class="fr">el-kilab dol</span>
</details>

**4.** القطة ___ *(cat, f.)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>

</details>

**5.** الكرسي ___ *(chair, m.)*

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">ده</span>

</details>
